business_scope.primary_industry_name: Transcontinental Container Block Train Expedited Freight Forwarding

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French-influenced with constitutional and commercial codification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF creation, as amended by Ley 1121 de 2006); Decreto Único Reglamentario 1068 de 2015, Libro 1, Título 4 (AML/CFT measures); Decreto 830 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB); Circular Externa 100-000005 de 2021 de la Superintendencia de Sociedades; Ley 1258 de 2008 (SAS regime).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuance authority in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of foreign corporate shareholder or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority (e.g., IRS, HMRC, SAT) in the jurisdiction of tax residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified power of attorney for incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, legal representatives, directors, and initial shareholders shall be screened against: (i) UIAF national terrorist financing list; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list; (iii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (v) Colombian Procuraduría General's disciplinary data; (vi) Interpol Red Notices; and (vii) Colombian domestic PEP dataset published by the Secretary of Transparency. PEP identification covers heads of state, ministers, congress members and senators, high-court justices, generals of police and military, ambassadors, and central-bank board members, as well as their spouses, children, and close associates. Enhanced due diligence and country-risk assessment are mandatory for foreign-incorporated beneficial owners; all screening results must be archived in the corporate AML file with date and source references.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rues.org.co), administered by the local Cámara de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Spanish or in transliterated Latin alphabet equivalents, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name in the same commercial registry. The distinctive element may be a word, phrase, or trademark demonstrable in Spanish; foreign-language words are accepted only if the applicant files a Spanish explanatory text in the articles of incorporation. The corporate suffix 'S.A.S.' must appear immediately after the registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Cámara de Comercio rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration with the same Cámara de Comercio within five (5) business days, attaching the original homonímicos certificate and evidence of grace-period entitlement. If the rejection persists, the applicant may submit an appeal to the Superintendencia de Sociedades pursuant to Article 79 of Código de Procedimiento Administrativo y de lo Contencioso Administrativo (Ley 1437 de 2011), requesting review within fifteen (15) business days. In all cases, the reserved name must be reused after the 30-day hold ends; otherwise a new reservation must be obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are accepted for correspondence and administrative service, but the company must maintain a physical Colombian location (domicilio) capable of receiving judicial notices and DIAN notifications. In the logistics and freight forwarding sector, a virtual office alone may trigger heightened commercial-substance scrutiny; a docu-drop service combined with local designated personnel will satisfy the minimum practical requirement but is not a substitute for a dedicated operational address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40–60% unannounced inspection probability during the first 24 months, driven by DIAN and Superintendencia de Sociedades monitoring of freight-forwarding and logistics entities, with particular attention to intermodal rail operations and consequent transfer-pricing and customs-risk profiles.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search, clearance, and reservation certificate (Cámara de Comercio)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff fixed by Cámara de Comercio pursuant to Decree 1074 de 2015

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for S.A.S. pre-incorporation legal services, including drafting, conflict-of-interest analysis, and shareholder agreement review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of shareholder passport, tax residence, and corporate status documents (per four documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the respective origin jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard Hague Apostille fee of approximately USD 15 per document in common jurisdictions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration tariff calculated based on initial capital amount under Decree 1074 de 2015 and municipal resolutions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for AML/KYC package, background screening, and management of documentary requirements

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Código de Comercio, arts. 353–372; Decreto 1074 de 2015 (RUES); DIAN Resolución 000033 de 2019 (SIA customs intermediation); Ley 336 de 1996 and Decreto 1530 de 1996 (multimodal transport)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce) through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES); tax registration via DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private instrument of incorporation and bylaws) filed with the Cámara de Comercio; elevación a escritura pública required when real property is contributed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital under Ley 1258 de 2008. Subscribed capital may be paid within two years; paid-in capital is evidenced by deposit into the corporate bank account. In-kind contributions of real estate require a public deed and registration in the Registro de Instrumentos Públicos.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. ONE — INAUGURAL BOARD RESOLUTION. WHEREAS the Sole Shareholder subscribed the entire authorised capital under Ley 1258 de 2008, IT IS RESOLVED: 1. The share subscription list and subscription payment plan are approved; all issued shares are validly issued. 2. The registered office is fixed at the corporate domicile, Carrera 7, Bogotá D.C., Colombia, and the statutory audit is dispensed as legally permitted. 3. The inaugural officers are appointed: President, Legal Representative, and Secretary; the Legal Representative receives full powers to appear before the Cámara de Comercio, DIAN, and financial entities. 4. The Board instructs the deposit of paid-up capital in the corporate account and the immediate commencement of incorporation formalities. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability, Homologation and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — RUES single-window web portal (https://www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the 'Certificado de Homologación de Nombre' application on the RUES platform. Select up to three alternative corporate names; the Chamber screens each proposed name against existing trademarks and registered company names. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 working days. Download the official reservation certificate and attach it to the incorporation file for submission in Step 3.
required_dossiers: RUES corporate name search and reservation form
Applicant's validated identity document (cédula/passport)
Power of attorney if filing through an appointed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is homologous to an existing registration, promptly file a new application indicating the second or third alternative. No fee is refunded for rejected names. The approved name certificate may be extended once for an additional 30 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation (Estatutos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public where real property is contributed; otherwise direct private execution before the Cámara de Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the estatutos sociales containing: corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose aligned to ISIC 5229 (intermodal container block-train freight forwarding), duration, authorized capital and share classes, board and officer structure, and audit dispensation clause. Each subscriber signs with an inked fingerprint or by virtue of a power of attorney. If the capital contribution includes real estate, formalize the document as escritura pública, pay the notarial tariff, and register the property transfer in the Registro de Instrumentos Públicos.
required_dossiers: Draft estatutos (private incorporation document)
Copy of the approved name reservation certificate
Valid original ID of each subscriber
Property title and cadastral certificate for in-kind contributions (if any)
Notary fee payment receipt (if escritura pública is executed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects clauses contrary to Ley 1258 de 2008 or the Commercial Code, amend the offending articles, obtain re-execution of signatures, and either re-notarize or convert the private instrument into a public deed before resubmission to the Chamber.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Mercantile Registry and Issuance of Legal Existence Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio — Registro Mercantil (local Chamber office or RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation document along with the RUES basic and supplementary forms and the pre-RUT issued by DIAN. Pay the registration tariff, bulletin tariff, and commercial registry book fees. The Chamber verifies statutory compliance and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which confers juridical personality. The Company is automatically enrolled in RUES, the municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA) registry, and the national corporate information repository.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución (original and copy)
Certificate of name reservation
RUES basic form and supplementary (complementario) form
Pre-RUT or pending NIT application code
Proof of payment of registration tariffs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a query (observación) for missing clauses, illegible signatures, or incomplete forms, cure the defect within 30 calendar days via a supplementary board resolution; corrected documents are re-submitted without loss of the original filing priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive Tax Registration at DIAN — NIT, RUT, and Electronic Invoicing Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the temporary NIT printed on the Chamber certificate, file the definitive RUT (Registro Único Tributario) through MUISIE. Select the applicable tax responsibilities: income tax, VAT, ICA retention, national stamp tax, and self-retention. Request digital signature activation and enroll in the electronic invoicing system either through a certified software provider or DIAN's free invoicing tool. Validate the registered address and download the definitive RUT reflecting status 'INSCRITO'.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Pre-RUT form
Legal representative identity document and professional ID (certus)
Utility bill or lease contract proving registered address
Digital signature issuance request (certificado digital)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax responsibility code is missing or DIAN assigns incorrect tariffs, file a corrective 'Actualización RUT' within the same MUISIE session. Voluntary correction before any formal requirement avoids penalties; DIAN resolves the update in up to 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Social Security / ARL Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (regulated credit institutions); EPS and ARL administrators registered with the Ministry of Health and Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking or savings account in a supervised financial entity and deposit the subscribed paid-in capital. Submit the final beneficiary sworn statement (Beneficiario Final). Register the Company as employer in the PILA electronic payroll system, subscribe the occupational risk insurance (ARL) policy corresponding to risk class II for the ISIC 5229 freight forwarding operation, and enroll the legal representative and employees with the chosen EPS and pension fund.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Definitive RUT and NIT
Bylaws and first board resolution appointing officers
List and identity documents of final beneficiaries
ARL quotation and PILA employer registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence under SFC Circular 004 de 2022, provide the final beneficiary certificate and full corporate chain disclosure. If the ARL rejects the declared risk class, reclassify the activity per Resolution 1111 de 2017 / Decreto 1072 de 2015 criteria and submit a rectified PILA form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Operating Permits: Aduanera Authorization (SIA) and Multimodal Transport Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN — Subdirección de Gestión de Aduanas; Ministerio de Transporte — Dirección de Transporte Ferroviario y Masivo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration as Sociedad de Intermediación Aduanera (SIA) with DIAN if customs brokerage is part of the intermodal service. Separately, register the Company as a multimodal transport operator with the Ministry of Transport under Decreto 1530 de 1996, presenting cargo liability insurance, rail network usage agreements, and proof of financial capacity. After approval, enroll in the Registro Nacional de Empresas de Transporte and publish the operating authorization in the Chamber of Commerce records.
required_dossiers: SIA application form and annexes per DIAN Resolución 000033 de 2019
Registro de operador de transporte multimodal form
Certificado de Existencia, bylaws, and NIT
Cargo liability insurance policy certificate
Financial capacity statement with bank references and contracts with railway operators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Transport questions technical capacity, supplement the filing with executed rail corridor access or subcontract agreements with certified line operators. The applicant may file the recurso de reposición appeal within 10 working days of any adverse administrative decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Transporte — Dirección de Transporte Ferroviario y Masivo; DIAN — Subdirección de Gestión de Aduanas (SIA); Agencia Nacional de Infraestructura (ANI) for rail terminal concessions
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Habilitación como Operador de Transporte Multimodal and Registro como Sociedad de Intermediación Aduanera (SIA); Registro Nacional de Empresas de Transporte under Ley 336 de 1996

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA), with local Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) jurisdiction for warehouse and transfer yard operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — No full Environmental Impact Assessment for pure ISIC 5229 freight forwarding and administrative offices. A full EIA is triggered only for construction of rail intermodal terminals exceeding Decreto 1076 de 2015 thresholds (e.g., cargo handling ≥ 150,000 tonnes/year or land disturbance > 2 ha). Otherwise a Declaración de Cumplimiento Ambiental and registration with the CAR suffices.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Resolución 0631 de 2015 for wastewater discharges (pH 6.0–9.0; BOD5 ≤ 200 mg/L; TSS ≤ 100 mg/L for non-domestic effluents), VOCs per Resolución 909 de 2008 (allowable emission factors for diesel handling and transfer equipment), and hazardous waste manifesting per Resolución 1407 de 2014 through licensed gestores.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos via the SOFIA-Plus platform; structural load and traffic impact approval from the local Curaduría Urbana when adapting container yards or warehouse facilities; occupational health and safety clearance under Decreto 1072 de 2015 (SG-SST) with ARL registration; civil defense certificate evidencing employee emergency evacuation drills and emergency response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), Bogotá D.C.; online portal: https://www.dian.gov.co (MUISCA self-service platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Colombian S.A.S. (foreign-owned): (1) register incorporation at the Chamber of Commerce; (2) apply for RUT inscription through DIAN's MUISCA portal using the legal representative's digital certificate; (3) obtain NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) upon approval; (4) update RUT to register as Responsable de IVA if conducting taxable activities or exports; (5) activate customs and foreign-exchange statuses, including 'exportador'. A non-domiciled foreign entity may obtain a non-resident NIT through a designated agent, but this dossier assumes the Colombian S.A.S. is the operating exporter.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election is available. An S.A.S. is a Colombian domestic corporation taxed at the entity level. The only optional regime relevant to eligibility is the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE), available when annual gross revenue does not exceed 100,000 UVT and the business activity is eligible; ordinary VAT and corporate income tax otherwise apply mandatorily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) — Colombian value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold: any person, including a S.A.S., performing taxable activities in Colombia must obtain RUT/IVA registration before the first taxable event. Occasional sellers of tangible goods are subject to IVA registration only above 15,200 UVT; for the optional SIMPLE regime the annual revenue ceiling is 100,000 UVT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronics invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta) via DIAN-authorised software or direct API. Each invoice must be transmitted in XML to DIAN's validation services in near-real time; the invoice must receive an accepted/valid status, include the CUDE (Código Único de Facturación), and carry a QR code. In rail-freight and intermodal forwarding, additional electronic transport documents and the electronic support document for acquisitions from non-obligated parties may be required. Failure to comply triggers penalties under Articles 652 and 652-1 of the Colombian Tax Statute.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Sales of goods that physically leave Colombian customs territory are treated as excluded from IVA (0% effective rate), provided the export is duly completed and evidenced. Export services, including international freight-forwarding and rail intermodal transport services, are zero-rated under Article 481 of the Tax Statute where the service is performed for use or consumption abroad. The exporter must be the legal owner of the goods, hold RUT status as Responsable de IVA, and maintain the physical and financial evidence of the export operation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación DEX) accepted and transmitted by DIAN
Bill of Lading or Multimodal Bill of Lading for rail intermodal movement
International rail waybill (CIM/SMGS) or combined transport bill evidencing the route to customs exit
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de compensación de divisas / Formulario No. 1)
Certificate of origin or transport authorization if a preferential trade claim is made
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may verify physical customs exit, delivery to the foreign acquirer, and actual repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days. Any improper VAT refund is clawed back with default interest; fraudulent requests trigger the penalty for inexactness (100% of the improper benefit), an additional 30% penalty for improper refunds, possible criminal liability for customs fraud under Law 1762 of 2015, and cancellation of export-registration status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia); foreign exchange surveillance and enforcement is exercised through the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, while the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit issues exchange policy guidelines under Law 9 of 1991 and Decree 1735 of 1993.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates an officially free foreign exchange market embedded in a regulated framework. Current account payments and transfers are freely convertible and may be processed through authorized local banks without prior central bank approval, subject only to documentary verification. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, foreign loans, and portfolio investments, are freely permitted but require mandatory registration with Banco de la República for statistical, tax, and future repatriation purposes. Profit and dividend remittances are lawful once the foreign investment has been duly registered and the applicable corporate income tax (31% statutory rate) has been settled; a certificate of tax compliance from DIAN may be required. Residual restrictions exist only in respect of non-registered investments and transactions that do not pass through the formal exchange market, which would expose the company to exchange infractions. Overall convertibility risk for an operating S.A.S. is low, while documentation discipline is mandatory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be channeled (canalización) through the foreign exchange market using an authorized intermediario del mercado cambiario. For goods exports, the exporter must repatriate and realize or deposit the FX proceeds within six (6) months from the date of the export declaration (Declaración de Exportación) or the shipment date, whichever applies; an extension of up to three (3) additional months may be requested before expiry. Service exports, including rail freight forwarding ancillary services, have a twelve (12) month channeling term. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into COP; the exporter may keep the proceeds in a local foreign currency deposit account, provided the funds are settled through a local bank and the respective FX declaration is submitted. Non-compliance triggers fines and the inability to deduct certain expenses connected to the export transaction until the channeling obligation is regularized.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability; Medium only under a local licensed partnership. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not recognized as authorized financial entities in Colombia; banking and monetary intermediation activities are reserved for entities licensed by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC). Unregulated EMIs cannot open local nostro accounts, issue payment instruments, or execute FX transactions in the official exchange market. They may provide invoice automation, treasury software, and conduit payment technology, but any settlement must occur through a Colombian licensed bank or an SFC-authorized payment company. The account-holding bank will treat such EMI as a third-party service provider subject to separate KYC and contractual review.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the legal representative or a duly authorized officer is generally required for corporate account opening, especially where the S.A.S. is owned by non-resident shareholders. Under the Colombian legal framework, banks implement in-person identification and signature verification in accordance with SFC rules; however, some tier-one banks accept hybrid remote opening: video interview for identity confirmation, submission of apostilled corporate documents, and subsequent in-person activation or correspondent bank authentication. For the low-risk rail freight forwarding profile (ISIC 5229), remote first-step onboarding may be accepted, but final account activation normally requires the physical meeting of the appointed local legal representative or an individual with a notarized and apostilled power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layer ownership chain involving foreign shareholders in high-risk or tax-secrecy jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate diagram to beneficial owners; certified copies of passports and residence documents; apostilled and notarized bylaws (estatutos) and certificate of incorporation from the Cámara de Comercio; board resolution appointing account signatories; source of wealth statement with supporting contracts, bank references, and audited financial statements when the capital contribution exceeds the bank's threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening alert triggered by inbound capital routed through a jurisdiction with restrictive FX or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/UNSC sanctions screening report and negative hits explanation; legal opinion from Colombian counsel confirming the lawful origin of funds; copies of bilateral or freight-transit contracts evidencing the commercial substance; intermediate ownership registry and ultimate beneficial owner declaration; sworn statement that funds are free of encumbrances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Freight forwarding payments involving unrelated third-party payables, port charges, and rail terminal costs appearing as potential trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying transport contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, railway consignment notes, container tracking records, terminal handling receipts, DIAN customs declarations, and matching payment orders showing a coherent cash-flow trail; documented treasury policy for segregation of duties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the registered corporate purpose and actual cross-border intermodal logistics activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated objecto social expressly covering rail freight forwarding and intermodal logistic services; ISIC/NAICS classification certificate; concession agreements or signed subcontracts with licensed rail operators; forecast cash-flow statement aligned with freight orders; professional references from logistics industry counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing: the foreign investor transmits the capital contribution via SWIFT MT103 from an offshore bank account to the Colombian S.A.S.'s account at an authorized local bank. The remittance must refer to the Colombian NIT (tax identification number) and clearly indicate the investment concept, e.g., 'Foreign Direct Investment – Capital Contribution'. Upon receipt, the local bank will classify the transaction as a capital account operation and require the execution of a foreign exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales). The company must register the investment with Banco de la República within one (1) year of the effective contribution, through the bank or directly via the electronic system of the central bank. The registration includes the investor's identity, the amount in COP and foreign currency, the established equity percentage, and the sector classification. Evidence required: apostilled incorporation documents, board resolution approving the capital call, bank statement of the remittance, and a sworn statement from the legal representative. Without registration, profit remittance and eventual disinvestment are unavailable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for freight and intermodal rail operations are cleared through: (a) SWIFT MT103 direct bank wires for freight charges, terminal fees, storage, and ancillary logistics payments to foreign counterparties; (b) commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) issued by Colombian banks in favor of rail operators or equipment suppliers, governed by UCP600 and ISP98 rules; (c) documentary collections (D/P, D/A) as secondary support instruments. Each convertible outbound payment must pass through the exchange market if remitted in foreign currency; the bank will require underlying commercial contracts, invoices, customs evidence (where applicable), and the corresponding form for the exchange declaration. Payments to related parties must comply with the OECD transfer pricing standard and the Colombian tax code to preserve deductible treatment; the financial institution may require a corporate resolution and due diligence on the recipient's ultimate beneficial owner.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cobertura en forwards deliverable (Delivery Forwards) COP/USD and COP/EUR with local authorized banks
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referenced to the TRM or official guide rate for hedgers lacking COP cash flows
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) between COP/USD and COP/EUR for balance-sheet and cash-flow hedging
FX Options (European style) on COP/USD for freight cost volatility management
Interest Rate Swaps combined with FX forwards for financing or leasing of rail assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than March 31 each year based on registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge equivalent to 1.5% of registered net assets per month or fraction; repeated delinquency can trigger administrative strike-off and cancellation of commercial registration after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed annually by DIAN Resolution based on the last two digits of the NIT; generally between mid-April and mid-May for calendar year-end entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of tax due plus daily interest arrears; continued non-filing permits tax authority default assessment, bank-account freezing, and fines or criminal exposure for willful evasion; does not directly cause corporate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; shareholder approval required no later than March 31, effectively creating an April 30 annual deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to 15 Tax Value Units (UVT) for late or non-filing; company loses evidentiary standing for financial documents and may be marked as in dissolution or dormant when paired with registry non-renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Registry Annual Update (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the annual corporate income tax return deadline; any share or beneficial-ownership change requires a separate update within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from 1,200 to 35,000 UVT (approx. COP 56 million to COP 1.6 billion) for failure to report, late reporting, or false information; non-reporting does not trigger automatic administrative strike-off but can suspend share transfer effectiveness.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of Revisor Fiscal if gross assets at December 31 exceed 5,000 UVT (approx. COP 235 million / USD 59,000), or if gross revenue in the prior year exceeds 5,000 UVT; also mandatory if required by tax law, regulatory rules, or when the S.A.S. issues securities to the public.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia (Decreto 2420 de 2015, and subsequent amendments): Full IFRS for Grupo 1; IFRS for SMEs for Grupo 2; simplified Colombian GAAP for Grupo 3 micro-entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RUB beneficial-owner registry requires an annual reaffirmation submitted before the income tax return due date; share transfers and any indirect ownership changes must be reflected in the Register of Members and reported through the DIAN UBO module within 30 days; a no-change confirmation is permitted only after affirmatively declaring the absence of any new beneficial owner.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday applies to ISIC 5229 rail freight expediting. The S.A.S. may use narrow statutory deductions and exemptions (e.g., charitable deductions, renewable-energy investments, or a 20% Zona Franca rate) only if facts qualify; absent such drivers, the effective rate is at or near 35%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically via DIAN's MUISCA portal (www.dian.gov.co) with digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Colombia operates a calendar fiscal year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due in September of the following tax year, with exact date assigned by the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT; for tax year 2024 the filing window generally runs from 10 to 30 September 2025, i.e., approximately nine months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from intermodal rail freight expediting, including transport brokerage, block train coordination, drayage, customs facilitation and forwarding fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Colombian-resident entity revenue in COP; non-resident shareholders have no filing obligation on this return. Foreign-currency invoicing for cross-border rail services must be translated at the Bank of the Republic exchange rate on the accrual date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Returns, rebates, price adjustments and discounts granted to clients; netted against gross revenue when supported by valid invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep contractual addenda, credit notes and customs documents in the TP file. Discounts issued to related non-resident rail carriers must satisfy the arm's-length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income (renta líquida gravable) after allowed costs, deductions and tax-loss offsets; the base to which the 35% corporate rate is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: DIAN TP adjustments may increase this figure if the S.A.S. charges below-market fees to non-resident railway affiliates. The non-resident ultimate beneficiary is not taxed on this line, but dividend distributions will be separately withheld.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable at the 35% statutory rate, reduced by prepayments, withholdings and foreign tax credits validly claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the entity-level tax; it is not offset by any credits standing in the hands of non-resident shareholders. The S.A.S. must remit the balance to DIAN through authorized financial entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable withholdings (retenciones) on income suffered during the year, including charges on railway freight contracts and bank interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach DIAN withholding certificates. Withholding relating to non-resident counterparties without a permanent establishment is not credited on this line; instead, the S.A.S. must pay over such withholdings as a withholding agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty of 5% of the income tax payable per month or fraction of month, capped at 100% of the tax due; zero-tax filers attract a minimum late-filing penalty of 0.5% of gross equity or gross income, whichever is greater. Late payment additionally accrues DIAN default interest (currently approximately 1.2% per month).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced dividend withholding rate under a Colombian tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the paying S.A.S. (i) a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) issued by the foreign tax authority, (ii) a Beneficial Ownership statement, and (iii) the applicable treaty form. The withholding agent must retain the documentation, include the distribution in Form 2276, and cite the treaty only if the conditions are continuously satisfied; relief usually depends on ownership percentage and beneficial-owner status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for trademarks, patents, software and similar IP paid to non-residents: statutory 15%; treaty rates usually 5%–10%. Cross-border interest: statutory 15%, treaty-reduced where applicable; Colombia does not impose an interest deduction restriction without compliance with thin-capitalization and CFC rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation and Form 120 declaration are required when taxpayer gross income or net equity exceeds 450,000 UVT (approximately COP 21,178,500,000 for tax year 2024) and related-party cross-border transactions exceed 20,000 UVT per counterparty; documentation must include Local File and, if applicable, Master File in Spanish.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the DIAN enforces general anti-abuse and substance-based norms (E.T. Article 869), the abuse-of-law doctrine and BEPS minimum standards. The rail-freight S.A.S. must demonstrate genuine economic activity—actual subcontracts, container tracking systems, trained personnel, office premises and commercial risk—or face income re-attribution, denial of treaty benefits and characterization as an artificial intermediary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematic understatement of block-train and intermodal forwarding revenue, fabrication of carrier costs, or issuance and receipt of false transport invoices to inflate deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN penalty of 100%–200% of the understated tax, plus adjusted taxable income, default interest and possible tax fraud criminal prosecution under Colombian Criminal Law (Ley 1762/2015) carrying imprisonment of 36–108 months and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who sign falsely or order concealment are jointly and severally liable under E.T. Article 793; civil restitution of evaded tax, personal asset attachment, travel suspensions and entry bans to Colombia, potential extradition, and disqualification as officers in any Colombian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. with no physical presence, employees, freight documents or operational control, using it solely to invoice foreign clients and park profits before repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the corporate personality under general anti-abuse rules, reallocate income to the foreign controlling party, assess 200% penalties on non-deductible costs, and cancel the mercantile registration in the Cámara de Comercio.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominal shareholders and founders face de facto manager liability, tort claims from creditors, criminal liability for ideological falsehood in incorporation, and a ban on holding corporate directorships in Colombia.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving freight settlement payments in cash or cryptocurrency, structuring wire transfers to evade reporting, or using the rail expediting platform as a pass-through for undocumented Swift/LOC remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial Superintendency fines up to COP 32 billion or 10 times the illicit transaction; asset freezing, business dissolution, and criminal money-laundering charges (Criminal Code Article 323) carrying 96–270 months imprisonment and monetary fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers executing or concealing such transfers face criminal complicity, personal forfeiture of Colombian assets, restriction orders preventing exit from Colombia, Interpol-driven extradition and multi-jurisdictional asset freezing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 120 or Local/Master File; charging non-arm's-length consolidated fees or dispatch coordination services to foreign rail affiliates; failure to justify allocation of intermodal operating costs to Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN transfer-pricing adjustment, penalty of 5%–10% of the transaction value or 100%–300% of the adjustment, plus moral interest; the taxpayer loses the right to present reliable evidence after the inspection notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false transfer-pricing certifications or causing the omission may be jointly liable for the additional corporate tax; repeated non-compliance may trigger a DIAN criminal referral and a personal judicial garnishment order.
